citations.linguistic_note: Proposed maritime-to-garage hypothesis (Italian/Sicilian scialuppa ~ cialuppa and North American French chaloupe mapped onto pre-1924 U.S. garage 'old boat / old tub' slang, with possible reinforcement from Scots gilpy and Yiddish shlape/shlap). Brookline's 1921–1925 fictional prep-school names ('East Jolopy / Jalopy / Gillopie Prep.') and local Ford-trade context are classified separately from the 1927–1930 automotive attestations; neither proves the source of the first syllable.
citations.analysis_notes: Contextual prosopography (neither advertisement contains 'jalopy'/'jolopy'): Louis A. Vachon Sr.'s Brookline Ford dealership explicitly advertised 'OLD CARS TAKEN IN TRADE' in the 1919 Blue Book of Brookline (p. 2, leaf n5) and ran an authorized Ford dealer ad on p. 305 (leaf n336) of the exact June 1921 Sagamore Graduation Number carrying Arthur A. Leonardi's 'East Jolopy Prep.' (CERT-1900-103). The 1922 Brookline directory and 1930 municipal street list link Louis A. Vachon Sr., Leonardi's 1921 classmate/historian Regina C. Vachon (who lists 'flivvering' and 'To have a real car for myself' on p. 265, leaf n296, and appears driving two Fords in the class prophecy on p. 243, leaf n274), and 1925 'East Gillopie Prep.' contributor Louis A. Vachon Jr. (CERT-1900-201) to the household at 633 Washington Street. These sources make a Brookline used-car pun plausible without proving what the fictional prep-school name meant, selecting among etymological derivations, or equating a Maine St. Dominique hockey player surnamed Vachon in a 1923 Bates report with Louis Jr.
